holder-quote: Behind the two, stomping along and muttering into his beard, was Dawil, a Dwarf [Axe Champion] dressed in full plate armor.
She pointed at Dawil. The Dwarf blinked at her accusatory finger.
Dawil finished his story as he spoke to Falene, Ylawes, Yvlon, Ceria, and Ksmvr. The other adventurers nodded without much enthusiasm. Only Ksmvr seemed animated.
The [Axe Champion] sighed gustily. He looked up at Ylawes and shook his head.
I just wish I didn’t have this damn [Axe Champion] class. Why couldn’t it have been a hammer throwing competition?
The half-Elf [Battlemage] flicked her fingers at the [Axe Champion] and [Knight]. Ylawes sensed the silence engulf Falene and her horse. He glanced at Dawil.
Dawil caught himself. Falene wasn't in the mood for their regular sparring sessions.
“I don’t know. I was hoping you knew. Dawil thought it was some old coin. Maybe a medallion or something fancy from another age?”
Dawil glanced up sharply. But Ylawes said nothing more. Falene nodded. After a moment, the [Axe Champion] cleared his throat.
Dawil had removed his axe. The [Axe Champion] lifted it.
That was all Pelt demanded. He didn’t offer Dawil anything; the [Axe Champion] hesitated. And then slowly unhooked the axe he treasured and carried everywhere and placed it on the table.
“That’s a good idea, Dawil. I’m glad someone has their priorities straight.”
Dawil gave Trey a steady gaze, which the young man returned. He saw what Cognita was—or a different side of her, like Trey. The Gold-rank [Axe Champion] settled back.
Ylawes wanted Dawil to use the potion, but the [Axe Champion] had refused
